Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

longē

adverb

far, a long way (off); by far (with superlatives)

In this lexicon

  • far

    the recommended word · classical · Ov. Ars 2.10: longē quem petō portus abest; Cic. Quinct. 79: quam longē est hinc in saltum Gallicānum? (Lewis & Short)

  • far

    also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.5.89: pānis longē pulcherrimus; Ter. Ad. 1.1.40: errat longē (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • quid properās, juvenis? mediīs tua pīnus in undīs nāvigat, et longē quem petō portus abest

    why the hurry, young man? your ship is out in mid-sea, and the harbour I’m making for is far awayOv. Ars 2.9–10

    In the entry for far

  • 'nihil,' inquit, 'longē est deō'

    ‘nothing,’ she said, ‘is far from God’Aug. Conf. 9.11.28

    In the entry for far

  • vēnit vīlissima rērum hīc aqua, sed pānis longē pulcherrimus

    here water, the cheapest thing there is, is sold for money; but the bread is by far the finestHor. S. 1.5.88–89
